**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes the request origin back only if the origin is one of these:
- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- anything ending in `.pages.dev`, at any depth
- anything ending in `.workers.dev`, at any depth

A request with no `Origin` header gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. Every other origin is also rejected with `null`.

The same middleware allows methods `GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS` and headers `Content-Type, Authorization`, with `maxAge: 86400`. It applies to all routes (`'*'`), including `/api/health`.

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if (...)` condition inside that `origin` function at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add one more `||` clause with the full origin, for example `origin === 'https://app.example.com'`. Use an exact match with the scheme included, not a bare hostname.

Don't add it to an array. The comment at line 20 says Hono matches array entries as exact strings only. `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` says the same and points to DEPLOYMENT_NOTES §4.

Avoid a loose `endsWith('example.com')` check, because it would also match `evilexample.com`. If you need wildcard subdomains, use `endsWith('.example.com')`.

Redeploy the Worker after the change. `worker/wrangler.toml` holds only bindings (`AI`, `SESSION_KV`, `DB`, `ENVIRONMENT`), not CORS settings.

I read only `AGENTS.md`, the `index.md` doc and `index.ts`. I didn't check whether the frontend has its own API base URL setting that would also need updating for the new domain.
